jobs.title: Test Development Engineer
jobs.text: Role details Business / location: NanoAnalysis, High Wycombe Role: Test Development Engineer Reports to: Manufacturing Engineering Manager Direct reports: None Primary purpose Develop, implement and maintain automated and manual test solutions to ensure electronic products and sub-assemblies are correctly manufactured and perform to specification. Maintain and improve test fixtures and test methodologies, with the aim of automating testing as much as possible. Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Engineering to develop and improve test processes and methodologies. Key responsibilities Design, develop and support functional test solutions, hardware and software, for electronic assemblies and systems. Develop automated test programs using ATE platforms. Write, modify, debug and validate production test software. Configure and integrate electronic instrumentation including oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, electronic loads, spectrum analysers and DAQ systems. Develop and maintain test documentation including plans, SOPs and reports. Analyse production test data for trends, shifts and anomalies across products and manufacturing sites; generate and present summary reports. Work cross-functionally with manufacturing, design, quality and subcontract suppliers to implement corrective actions resulting from data analysis. Review test data and equipment usage statistics to identify preventative strategies and reduce long-term risk. Work with product design teams on DfM and DfT during new product development. Provide technical input into manufacturing/test strategy including capacity planning, supplier process capability and new-supplier evaluation. Act as a technical contact for subcontract electronics manufacturers and support production-test problem solving. Improve test efficiency, coverage, reliability and throughput. Ensure compliance with applicable safety and regulatory standards. Feed back on product testability, coverage, diagnosability, reparability, firmware/diagnostics, user experience, test time and yield. Interpret electrical diagrams and electronic schematics and relate them to the physical product. Indicative performance measures Departmental objectives/tasks achieved on time. COPQ and waste reduction. Inventory control via MRP transactions. 5S adherence and Kaizen improvements. TPM: equipment maintained, calibrated and in good working order. Work within the Quality policy/system. Health & Safety compliance. Person specification Education / experience Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering or related field, or equivalent experience. 5+ years’ experience in test development for electronics and related products. Professional skills / abilities Strong electronic test-equipment experience: oscilloscopes, DMMs, programmable PSUs, electronic loads, signal generators, etc. Hands-on ATE experience. Test-software development/debugging: examples include ATEasy, C/C++, C#, Python or similar. Analogue and digital electronics understanding and applicable test techniques. Hardware/software troubleshooting in a production test environment. Communications: CAN, SPI, I2C, RS-232/485, Ethernet, etc. Strong analytical/problem-solving skills. Soldering/desoldering of assemblies and PCBAs. Basic electrical wiring, termination, soldering and crimping. SMT repair/rework. Mains-powered equipment awareness and associated safety risks. Component-level PCBA fault finding. Assemble prototype test jigs/fixtures from engineering documentation/sketches. Automated test-data analysis tools, e.g. WATS. Personal qualities Strong written/oral communication and ability to influence internal/external customers at different organisational levels. Energy and positive attitude. Tenacity and desire to make a difference. Ability to motivate others and manage conflict to successful resolution. Resilience to production-environment pressures. Ability to manage multiple projects/priorities and provide quick-turnaround solutions to production stops. What the JD is really asking for The difficult engineering core is not manufacturing administration. It is an engineer who can move between the DUT, schematic, instruments, test fixture, software and production data; determine whether a failure is real or test-induced; automate the useful parts; and leave behind a repeatable production-capable test solution. The manufacturing-process items are still real requirements and should not be ignored; they are separated explicitly in the fit notes rather than being treated as equivalent to the technical core. Executive assessment The role is a strong match to the candidate’s practical electronics/test-development background. Best current estimate: Technical engineering core: approximately 93–97% match. Full literal JD/checklist: approximately 88–92% match. The strongest overlaps are ATE development, electronic instrumentation, automated measurement, production test, production-data analysis/reporting, PCBA/system fault-finding, embedded interfaces, Python/Tcl/SCPI/GPIB control, RF/analogue measurement and cross-domain debugging. The remaining weak-match areas are deliberately left explicit rather than rationalised away: WATS specifically: no direct experience evidenced. Formal supplier process capability / new-supplier evaluation: partial or adjacent experience, no formal ownership claimed. Capacity-planning ownership: no clear direct ownership evidenced. MRP / inventory transactions: no meaningful direct experience evidenced. Formal 5S / Kaizen / TPM ownership: no clear direct experience evidenced. Manufacturing / quality administration: partial; technical investigation is stronger than formal process ownership. Production-data analysis Recent interview-preparation recall established direct experience rather than merely transferable capability: Custom scripts to pull historical production-test results. Excel filtering/import by board revision, date, fitted options/configuration and batch. Batch-yield and revision-trend comparison. Investigation of messy BOM/revision/parts-change history to explain failures. Automated Excel templates/macros for CSV import. Word report generation per board/batch. Distinguishing normal variation and tester/calibration drift from genuine DUT changes. This directly supports the JD’s requirement to identify trends, shifts and anomalies and generate summary reports. Measurement / test-method judgement Examples include: Receiver sensitivity: learned the normal measurement envelope and avoided over-interpreting small (~0.3 dB) shifts within a much wider acceptable specification margin. VNA/test setup: identified one unit/setup drifting further out of calibration, explaining misleading red-herring data. IOBC procedure: recognised that assumptions about noise stability and cross-channel coupling did not reflect real behaviour; literal adherence could cause systematic false failures, implying the procedure itself required revision. Antenna S11: questioned whether secondary lobes in an uncontrolled/non-shielded room were repeatable DUT properties; small orientation changes affected traces enough to challenge their use as hard acceptance criteria. Better terminology is environmental/multipath/fixture-induced structure rather than strict signal-processing “aliasing”. Culture / company interpretation The technical environment appears hands-on and engineering-led beneath a larger corporate/manufacturing structure. The role explicitly spans PCBA test, fixtures, software, instrumentation, NPI, production transfer and suppliers rather than simple test execution. Main risk is not technical fit but management/process culture. The immediate Manufacturing Engineering Manager and local team are the most important unknowns to resolve in interview. Bottom line The role should be treated as a direct and unusually strong match to the difficult engineering content. It is not, however, a claim of prior mastery of WATS, MRP, formal supplier capability work, capacity planning, 5S/Kaizen/TPM or manufacturing administration. Those residual gaps remain transparent. Strongest role-fit examples End-to-end test solution ISS battery characterisation platform Complete practical test system spanning PCB/electronics, embedded firmware and Python UI/control. Strong example for a question asking about ownership from concept through usable test solution. Backups: IOBC test work; harness test work. ATE framework Etherstack RF validation automation Joined when formal RF validation had effectively no automation. Early Rx sensitivity process was manual: dump BER from debug console, paste into Excel, average, adjust signal-generator level, repeat. Initiated automation independently; it became the main role and eventually covered 100% of formal validation. Tcl scripts controlled instruments over SCPI/GPIB and interacted with DUT debug/configuration interfaces. Cisco/Ubiquisys is a strong backup: inherited a basic Perl/schema test framework; developed production-ready Rx sensitivity and adjacent-channel tests; used regression/best-fit logic to reduce noisy BER measurement time from minutes to seconds; transferred tests remotely to Foxconn. Multi-instrument integration / sequencing Etherstack full validation rack Rx and Tx test suites integrating signal generators, spectrum analysers, switching/routing and DUT control. Sequencing concerns included DUT state/configuration, stimulus setup, BER collection/averaging, binary/data downloads and reliable instrument state. Difficult production/test failure Etherstack enclosure-related Rx sensitivity degradation Degradation appeared only when the control board was installed in the final mechanical enclosure. Used BER logging, shielded-chamber testing, grounding/coupling investigation and configuration changes to isolate the physical cause. Final correction involved additional grounding plus RF absorber, restoring performance. Efficiency / throughput improvement Cisco/Ubiquisys receiver test Regression/best-fit approach handled noisy BER data efficiently. Reduced tests that took minutes to seconds and enabled rapid all-channel receiver characterisation. Factory deployment then returned useful production-yield data. Etherstack backup: grew automation to complete formal validation coverage. DfT / diagnosability Etherstack debug-console access, direct register/configuration control and BER reporting made faults more observable. Engineer-facing live BER Tk utility replaced repeated command/query/readback cycles. ISIS interface-board firmware rewrite removed dependency on obsolete production-test hardware and improved production continuity. Cross-functional corrective action / production-history investigation ISIS TRXVU crystal/BOM/revision issue Historical revision/BOM information was messy and nominal board revisions did not tell the whole story. Pulled and compared production records across parts changes/batches to reconstruct what had actually changed. Documented the findings and handed them to colleagues; formal quality-system work later became a deviation/work instruction. Correct framing: technical investigation/evidence reconstruction and documented handoff, not ownership of final QMS paperwork. Documentation / reproducibility Cisco/Ubiquisys to Foxconn Production tests were transferred remotely. A concise PDF memo/instruction was sufficient for the factory to run the tests successfully and start returning yield data. Etherstack backup: deployed and supported validated test setups in US/Canadian partner labs. Production-data analysis Direct evidence now established: scripts pulling archived production results; Excel import/filtering by revision/date/options/batch; batch-yield and revision-trend comparison; BOM/parts-change investigations; automated Excel templates/macros importing CSV data; Word reports per board/batch; distinguishing DUT trends from tester/calibration variation. Test-method judgement IOBC Documented assumptions about stable noise/cross-channel coupling did not match actual system behaviour. Literal application of the procedure could produce guaranteed/false failures. Raised the need to revise the test method/documentation rather than blindly enforce an invalid assumption. Antenna S11 / VNA Secondary S11 structure changed substantially with antenna orientation in an uncontrolled room. Questioned whether those lobes were repeatable DUT properties or environmental/multipath measurement structure. Was overruled, but the engineering lesson is to establish repeatability before using fine trace features as hard acceptance criteria. VNA calibration drift Compared measurement setups and identified one VNA/setup drifting more out of calibration, explaining anomalous red-herring data. Technical-question reminders Python ATE architecture DUT object and instrument/test-equipment objects. Test-case/test-sequence layer separate from drivers. Config/limits externalised via simple config or minimal GUI. Session logging separate from formal result CSV. Timestamped files with station/session/configuration metadata in headers. Clear instrument reset/init and error handling. I2C NACK debug Start physical/electrical before blaming software: power and rail integrity; pull-ups and logic levels; scope SDA/SCL for timing/non-standard behaviour; MCU/peripheral reset/state; then firmware timing, transaction sequencing, timeout/recovery logic. Spectrum analyser setup RBW, VBW, span, detector, attenuation and sweep time are coupled trade-offs. Choose settings from the signal bandwidth, required noise floor/dynamic range, whether the event is intermittent and required production throughput. Avoid blindly using maximum resolution when it only increases test time. SCPI over RS-232/Ethernet Design for: realistic operation-specific timeouts; termination/newline handling; IDN/connection validation; known/reset instrument state; stale buffers/partial responses; operation-complete or status checks where appropriate; reconnect/retry policy with bounded retries; useful communication/error logging. PCBA cold-pass / warm-fail establish power rails first with DMM/scope; profile relevant test points over time/temperature; trigger on rail dips/noise or fault onset; correlate failure with temperature and component/region where possible; separate DUT thermal drift from fixture/instrument/test-software effects. Mixed-signal PCBA fault finding Hierarchy: external supply/input power; main rails; enables/reset/clock/MCU boot; peripheral power/state; analogue signal chain; digital buses such as SPI only once prerequisites are known-good. High-current voltage droop verify electronic-load settings/limits and cabling first; measure voltage drop along PCB/cable path under load; check whether deltas make sense from R = V/I and P = VI; check current limiting/regulator behaviour and thermal rise; Eaton H-bridge work provides a real high-current anchor, including differential scope probing and loads up to ~10 A. Oscilloscope for intermittent interface faults trigger on the symptom/event if possible rather than free-run; use suitable probe loading/grounding; enough bandwidth/sample rate to see edge/timing issues, not just protocol-level states; deep memory for pre/post-trigger context; persistence/history/segmented capture for rare events; correlate digital fault with power/reset/enable lines when relevant. Production fixture design Direct classic bed-of-nails fixture ownership is not one of the strongest evidenced areas, so do not overclaim. The transferable approach is: use robust connectors/test points where available; choose pogo/bed-of-nails only where volume/access justify it; control cable length, grounding and shielding for analogue/RF signals; minimise contact resistance for power/high-current paths; add fixture self-test/loopback/reference checks where practical; key/interlock connections to reduce operator variability and incorrect mating. PSU + electronic-load sequencing start in a safe unloaded/current-limited state; initialise instruments and verify known state; apply supply, allow defined settling, verify rails before applying load; ramp/load in controlled steps where appropriate; monitor limits continuously and abort on unexpected voltage/current/temperature; on any exception remove load and power in a safe deterministic order; log the condition causing shutdown rather than simply returning FAIL. Transparent non-experience areas Do not try to disguise these in interview: no direct WATS experience evidenced; no meaningful MRP/inventory transaction experience evidenced; no formal ownership of 5S/Kaizen/TPM programmes evidenced; no formal supplier process-capability/new-supplier evaluation ownership evidenced; capacity-planning ownership not established; manufacturing/quality administration experience is lighter than hands-on engineering/problem investigation. Frame these as learnable surrounding processes, not as things already done. Oxford role hub Open the authoritative private issue, Markdown records and document attachments.

jobs.title: RF Validation Engineer
jobs.text: Role details Company: Qualinx Role: RF Validation Engineer Status: Historical / likely expired vacancy Original vacancy URL: https://qualinx.recruitee.com/o/rf-validation-engineer-2-4 Core role themes RF testing and validation; develop and execute test plans. Python and data analysis; automate tests and manage validation data. Lab equipment and automation; PXIe, analysers and oscilloscopes. Embedded systems and firmware; microcontrollers and SPI/I2C. Collaboration, documentation and reporting of findings. Bonus / optional areas GNSS. IoT. MATLAB. Keil. Source limitations Issue #1 retained only headline requirements plus the original vacancy URL. Exact reporting line, full location details, education requirements and other unretained advert text are intentionally not reconstructed. Executive assessment This is a close technical match to the established RF-validation / test-automation track. Strongest overlap: RF validation and test planning. Automated RF measurement and ATE development. Spectrum analysers, signal generators, VNAs, scopes and related lab equipment. SCPI/GPIB instrument control and scripting. Receiver sensitivity, BER/BLER and RF performance validation. Production and validation data handling/reporting. Firmware/DUT interaction through debug consoles, register access and MCU interfaces. SPI/I2C/UART familiarity and embedded-hardware awareness. Strongest direct evidence Etherstack Took RF validation from essentially no automation to complete formal validation coverage. Developed Tcl-based ATE controlling RF instrumentation over SCPI/GPIB. Automated receiver sensitivity, Tx/Rx validation and regression workflows. Performed hands-on RF debug, VNA-based matching/tuning, spectrum analysis and SMD rework. Supported test-system deployment and validation at partner labs in the US and Canada. Cisco / Ubiquisys Converted an existing Perl/schema test framework into production-ready LTE receiver sensitivity and adjacent-channel tests. Used regression/best-fit logic to accelerate noisy BER measurements from minutes to seconds. Supported RF switching, live BER visibility and remote factory handover to Foxconn. ISISpace Production test and debug of UHF/VHF CubeSat transceivers. Reworked legacy automation into a more robust validation environment. Developed targeted RF tests and worked at the firmware/hardware boundary, including I2C/UART interface-board firmware and PLL/VCO-related bring-up support. Data analysis / reporting Issue #58 adds direct evidence for production-data analysis and reporting: scripts to pull archived test results; Excel filtering by revision/date/configuration/batch; yield and revision trend comparison; automated CSV import/reporting flows; engineer-facing BER and batch reporting tools. This aligns well with the retained Qualinx requirement for Python/data analysis and management of validation results, although not every historical example used Python specifically. Adjacent rather than exact-match areas PXIe is named in the retained Qualinx summary; direct PXIe ownership is not clearly evidenced in the current notes. GNSS is listed as optional; no strong direct GNSS experience is currently evidenced. Keil is listed as optional; direct Keil use is not established in the retained evidence. MATLAB is directly evidenced at CSR, but it is an older part of the experience base. Python is directly used in later engineering/test systems, while the deepest RF ATE examples at Etherstack were Tcl and at Cisco/Ubiquisys Perl. Bottom line The role maps closely to the core career thread: RF bench validation plus automation, instrumentation, DUT interaction and result analysis. The strongest evidence is direct rather than merely transferable. The main gaps are platform/tool specifics such as PXIe, GNSS and Keil rather than the underlying validation work. Strongest examples Building RF validation automation from scratch Etherstack is the strongest example: joined when formal RF validation had effectively no automation; automated receiver-sensitivity and wider RF validation workflows; used Tcl with SCPI/GPIB-controlled RF instrumentation; expanded the framework until it covered the complete formal validation workload; combined automation with manual RF characterization and practical debug. Fast RF measurement / data handling Cisco/Ubiquisys: inherited a basic Perl/schema test framework; developed production-ready receiver-sensitivity and adjacent-channel tests; applied regression/best-fit logic to noisy BER measurements; reduced tests from minutes to seconds while enabling broad channel coverage; transferred the resulting factory test flow remotely to Foxconn. Embedded / firmware interaction Useful direct examples: Etherstack: debug-console commands, direct register reads/writes and XML configuration manipulation to control DUT states and inspect RF behaviour. ISISpace: I2C/UART interface-board firmware rewrite and targeted PLL/VCO bring-up support. Broader embedded work: PIC-based measurement/control systems and Python-controlled test platforms. RF debug case Etherstack enclosure-related receiver degradation: degradation appeared only in the final enclosure; BER logging and shielded-chamber testing helped isolate the issue; investigated grounding/coupling and mechanical configuration; grounding plus RF absorber restored performance. Validation data / reporting Direct examples retained in issue #58: historical test-result extraction; Excel filtering by revision/date/configuration/batch; trend and yield comparison; macro-assisted CSV imports and repeatable reports; live BER display tools for engineering debug. Likely discussion points Python versus older RF ATE languages Do not imply all RF automation was Python. The deepest RF ATE work used Tcl at Etherstack and Perl at Cisco/Ubiquisys. Python is nevertheless well established in later test-system and engineering work. Frame this as language-independent test architecture and rapid adaptation to the local toolchain. PXIe If asked, separate platform familiarity from underlying measurement competence. Direct PXIe ownership is not clearly retained in the current evidence, while RF instrumentation automation and measurement-system integration are strong. GNSS / IoT / Keil Treat these as optional/tool-specific areas unless direct evidence is recalled. Do not inflate them. Transparent gaps No clear direct PXIe ownership evidenced in current notes. No strong direct GNSS project evidence retained. No clear Keil-specific experience retained. Some strongest RF automation examples use Tcl/Perl rather than Python. These are narrower platform/tool gaps around an otherwise close RF validation match. Qualinx role hub Open the historical role issue, retained source reconstruction and supporting evidence.
